description.narrative:
Regional Asia Pacific Programme: Advancing Just Transitions to Climate Resilient and Nature-Positive Societies (RAPP2) is a regional program in Southeast Asia and South Asia run by RWI together with partners in the region. The intervention will last from May 2024 until December 2026.
RAPP2 is a continuation of Sida's previous support for RWI's Regional Asia Pacific Program (2017-2024). Sweden's support for RAPP2 is also a phase-out support for RWI's regional program in Asia and the Pacific.
RAPP2 builds on previous results from the regional program and strengthens capacity in South and Southeast Asia to achieve equitable and sustainable development. The overall objective of RAPP2 is to enhance enabling environments for just transitions to climate-resilient and nature-positive societies that are grounded in human rights and gender equality in the Asia-Pacific region. More specifically, RAPP2 will:
1) Strengthen the enabling environment for integrating and addressing human mobility risks, grounded in rights- and gender-based approach, in Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation (CCMA) Initiatives.
2) Strengthen the enabling environment for improved access to environmental justice in Southeast Asia.
3) Strengthen the enabling environment for increased business compliance with EU regulation on human rights and environmental due diligence in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors.
These objectives will be achieved by:
- strengthening universities' capacity to deliver evidence- and rights-based education in law, trade and extraction of minerals and biofuels, climate migration, and disaster risk reduction to the next generation of national and regional entrepreneurs, experts and leaders;
- strengthening the capacity of regional organizations and National Human Rights Institutes (NHRIs) to identify deficiencies and uphold environmental and human rights.
The Revision of the Philippines’ Procedural Rules on Environmental Cases is a smaller component of RAPP2 which is being conducted jointly with the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) and the Asia Research Institute on Environmental Law (ARIEL). The component lasts for one year (2024-2025). The component is a result of a call for proposals for deepened partnership among the existing partners to Sweden's regional development cooperation in Asia and the Pacific (2023-24 Idea Competition).

The overall objective of the second RWI Regional Asia Pacific Programme (RAPP2) is to enhance enabling environments for just transitions to climate-resilient and nature-positive societies that are grounded in human rights and gender equality in the Asia-Pacific region.
More specifically, RAPP2 will:
1) Strengthen the enabling environment for integrating and addressing human mobility risks, grounded in rights- and gender-based approach, in Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation (CCMA) Initiatives.
2) Strengthen the enabling environment for improved access to environmental justice in Southeast Asia.
3) Strengthen the enabling environment for increased business compliance with EU regulation on human rights and environmental due diligence in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors.

Some key results of the programme were achieved during the 8-month implementation period: RWI engaged 380 individuals engaged with and targeted by RAPP2. Of those engaged, 184 identified as female, 161 as male, and 35 preferred not to disclose their gender. Participants represented 57 diverse cross sections of institutions, including universities, law enforcement agencies, CSOs, embassies, and the private sector.
i) Strengthen the enabling environment for integrating and addressing human mobility risks, grounded in rights and gender based approach, in Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation (CCMA) Initiatives:
- In partnership with the Faculty of Legal Studies, South Asian University (FLSSAU) and Asia Pacific Forum (APF), RWI conducted a needs assessment and gap analysis of the targeted National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs). Results from the need assessment activities helped RWI and its partner co-develope monitoring toolkits (a module) to enable NHRIs to effectively monitor human rights issues in CCM initiatives, especially those related to the mobility dimensions to be concluded in 2025. RWI also assembled information from six South Asian NHRIs, including NHRI Bangladesh, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, particularly on the need for monitoring tools and techniques, and how to conduct the monitoring and evaluation activities at the national level.
This RWI developed toolkit responds to the gap by helping institutionalise HRBA to climate action, shifting the discourse from state-centric mitigation to one that emphasises the rights and vulnerabilities of individuals and communities. Equality (FIRE), developed by RWI and our partners, the toolkit aims to strengthen NHRIs technical knowledge and monitoring capacity to track states adherence to human rights obligations under climate change frameworks like the Paris Agreement.
- A gender based approach through transformative pedagogy in CCMA related courses was developed, as a result of training needs assessment conducted by RWI in collaboration with Manila University School of Law, which helped identification of the gaps and challenges to incorporate human rights and gender responsive notions in training modules to RAPP2 partners.
ii) Strengthen the enabling environment for improved access to environmental justice in Southeast Asia
- In partnerships with four national institutions in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand, RWI could develop a repository of case studies on transboundary environmental issues. In addition, through further collaboration with the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) as a regional partner, RWI could get support for both the development of the case repository and the design of case-based training modules. The Case Repository served as a vital resource for legal practitioners, civil society, justice sector actors, NHRIs, and the public.
This repository features an in-depth analysis of twelve landmark legal cases from Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines which revealed common barriers and gave access to rights-based litigation on climate change and transboundary environmental harm, including pollution of rivers and air. By showcasing both the gaps and good practices in environmental adjudication, the repository aims to inform future litigation strategies, support capacity building efforts, and promote more consistent application of human rights and gender equality principles in environmental decision making. It also offers a foundation for the development of training modules to prosecutors, lawyers, and NHRIs working across diverse jurisdictions in Southeast Asia.
iii) Strengthen the enabling environment for increased business compliance with EU regulation on human rights and environmental due diligence in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors.
In response to the environmental challenges associated with the just energy transition particularly the exploration of new energy sources that carry significant human rights risks, RWI convened a two-day workshop on the concept of Business, Human Rights, and the Environment (BHRE) in December 2024 in Indonesia, aiming at fostering cross-sector collaboration and curricular integration on the issue. The workshop brought together business academic institutions, especially those engaged in the critical minerals sector in Indonesia and biofuels in Cambodia, along with environmental and human rights civil society organisations.
As result from the workshop, RWI will establish formal collaboration with CamEd Business School Cambodia, PAHAM Law UNPAD from Indonesia, and Publish What You Pay (a CSO organization) in 2025 to integrate BHRE notion into business curricula. The results in this area as outcomes of the activities conducted in 2024 were essentially building knowledge bases, enhancing teaching capacity, and fostering transdisciplinary research collaborations in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors to integrate BHRE principles into academic curricula, ensuring that human rights and environmental sustainability are embedded in education and business practices.
iv) Enhance the environmental rule of law in the ASEAN region by promoting more efficient, effective, and accessible administration of justice in environmental matters. This outcome focused specifically on strengthening the enabling environment for Revision of the Philippines Procedural Rules on Environmental Cases: A Model for Regional Adoption.
Results in this area was focused on adopting an ecosystem based approach in environmental litigation, enhancing access to justice for Indigenous Peoples, strengthening the Writ of Kalikasan (a legal remedy in the Philippines designed to protect the constitutional right to a healthy environment) and Continuing Mandamus, and integrating human rights protections more effectively.
Two key activities were carried out: i) the National Climate Summit by the Supreme Court of the Philippines, held on 2829 November 2024, co-organised by RWI and ICJ, which convened 252 participants from across the Philippines' national judicial system and development partners with the discussion and key output recommendations to the revision of the RPEC; ii) A Regional Judicial Dialogue in September 2024 in Bangkok, Thailand was organized by RWI in collaboration with the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) and the Thailand Institute of Justice (TIJ). The event brought together 29 judges and legal professionals from six ASEAN countries Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, and the Philippines to share insights, lessons, and best practices on developing and applying procedural rules for environmental and climate change cases.
Insights garnered from the Focused Group Discussions with inputs to the National Climate Summit and the Regional Dialogue in Bangkok further enhanced the Revised Rules of Procedure provisions. The revision process will integrate feedback and recommendations from these engagements, ensuring the Rules of Procedure on Environmental Cases are aligned with current climate and human rights priorities in the Philippines.
v) Communication/Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)
A key highlight of RWI strategic communication and advocacy was a contribution to COP29 through four targeted deliverables, reinforcing its commitment to human rights-based approaches to climate action, particularly in Southeast Asia and in the context of climate mobility. This includes a side event on the ASEAN Environmental Rights Declaration, a panel on planned relocation and human rights, co-leading the UNFCCCs Paris Committee of Capacity Buildings (PCCB) 6th Capacity Building Hub thematic day on climate and mobility, and a capacity building session with SwedBio.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
